text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.38% today as oil markets strengthened on geopolitical risk. Brent crude topped $103 a barrel following reports that the U.S. is preparing for possible military operations against Iran, which would disrupt Middle East oil supplies—a major concern for global energy markets. The stock has climbed 1.37% over two weeks as these tensions have mounted, supporting higher crude prices that benefit oil producers.

The broader picture shows a widening gap between U.S. and global oil prices: domestic crude is trading at $96.24 while Brent (the global benchmark) sits at $125.44, a $29 spread driven partly by shipping bottlenecks in the Persian Gulf—supertanker rates have exploded to 10 times pre-war levels. This regional supply tightness is likely keeping upward pressure on the energy sector even as political pressure mounts domestically to address fuel prices.
